sections.html:
Valuing a parcel and collecting its tax are handled by different offices in Montgomery County. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) answers value questions. The Sheriff's Office prints and collects the bills.

  • PVA, (859) 498-8710: value, the tax roll and exemption forms.
  • Sheriff, (859) 498-8704: amounts due. Checks go to 1 Court Street, Suite 4, Mt. Sterling, KY 40353, with the bill number written on them.
  • County Clerk, (859) 498-8700: recording a deed, and any bill that has gone delinquent.

The sheriff's website lets you view and print bills and receipts but offers no way to pay online. If you want a receipt mailed back, enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope with the check.

The sheriff mails bills in the last week of September, and they become payable October 1. Each year the collection calendar runs like this:

Sheriff's collection calendar
DatesWhat the bill becomes
October 1 through November 1Two percent comes off
November 2 through December 31Printed total, no adjustment
January 1 through January 31Five percent is added
February 1 through April 15Twenty-one percent is added

A payment made while the 10% penalty applies, before the bill is handed to the clerk, carries one more 10% sheriff's fee. At close of business on April 15, delinquent bills transfer to the County Clerk. From then on a 20% County Attorney fee, a 10% clerk fee and 1% interest each month apply, and the clerk may sell a bill still unpaid to a third party in the summer.

A past-due bill belongs to the clerk after April 15, and the clerk gives the payoff. A seller who owes an earlier year should ask for that figure before picking a closing date. If your lender pays the tax from escrow, or a prior owner is responsible, the sheriff asks that you pass the bill along so it is paid on time.

sections.h2: Montgomery County housing and the market
sections.html:
The county covers 197 square miles of the Outer Bluegrass, with Mount Sterling as the seat, 34 miles east of Lexington. Clark County gave up the territory in 1796. The 2025 population is estimated at 28,822, a gain of 2.5% since 2020. Interstate 64 clips the north edge of town, and U.S. 60 and U.S. 460 cross downtown. The average commute is 25.7 minutes, and the area belongs to the Lexington combined statistical area.

There are 12,422 housing units, and 53 building permits were issued in 2025. Homeowners live in 68.3% of occupied units, leaving close to a third to renters. The midpoint of an owned home is $172,200, and renters pay a midpoint of $830 in gross rent. Ownership costs are $1,242 a month for mortgage holders and $470 for owners with no loan. A seller with deferred repairs can expect a slower sale than one with a tidy house.

Zoning is uneven. There is no countywide planning and zoning, yet subdivisions within five miles of Mt. Sterling must meet the city's zoning and subdivision rules. Anyone planning to split a lot before a sale should call city hall first. Court Day each October brings roughly 130,000 visitors downtown over four days, which is worth remembering before scheduling showings that weekend.

Values are pinned to January 1. Under KRS 133.120 the first step is a sit-down with the PVA or a deputy, which may be held by phone. KRS 133.045 opens the tax roll for inspection for 13 days from the first Monday of May, unless the Department of Revenue picks other dates.

If that talk fails, put your complaint in writing and deliver it to the County Clerk. Name the parcel, say why the number is wrong and state what you believe it is worth. The hearing is before the county appeals board, and the burden is on you to bring evidence such as an appraisal, listings or a builder's estimate.

While the case is open, pay on the value you claimed. A higher final number means you owe the gap plus interest. Skipping the county hearing forfeits the later route to the state Board of Tax Appeals.

The state exemption is $49,100 for tax years 2025 and 2026, open to anyone 65 or over or classified as totally disabled. It lowers the value that rates are applied to.

The PVA takes the form at (859) 498-8710. Age is shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claimants must reapply each year, with carve-outs for owners with a service-connected disability and for people whom Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has found permanently and totally disabled.

The owner on January 1 is the taxpayer for the whole year, so a house bought later still has its bill under the seller's name. KRS 134.015 calls the tax a personal debt of that owner. A lien from unpaid tax can last 11 years under KRS 134.420 and passes to the next buyer along with the land.

  • Ask the sheriff whether this year's bill is settled, and what payoff applies on the day of closing.
  • Decide in the sales contract who bears which months of tax.
  • Enter the buyer's address for later tax mailings on the deed, since KRS 382.135 demands it.
  • Record the signed deed at the County Clerk's office.

Title companies search for old bills, so paying any early prevents a hold-up at closing.

Owing tax doesn't block a sale. The payoff comes out of the proceeds at closing, so get a current figure from the sheriff, or from the clerk after April 15, and give it to the closing agent. If the bill has gone to the clerk, the attorney and clerk fees and monthly interest are part of that figure, and it rises each month, so ask for a figure dated near the closing day.

A cash sale as-is can suit an owner with deferred repairs, an inherited house or a bill already in collection, since it skips showings and lender repair demands. Bring the deed, your latest bill and, for an estate, the papers showing who may sign. After closing, the County Clerk records the deed, and the PVA should be told so the next bill reaches the new owner.

sections.h2: Getting a Montgomery County house ready to sell
sections.html:
Buyers here are often commuting toward Lexington, so exits 110 and 113 on Interstate 64 and the drive time from town are worth naming in a listing. The Montgomery County School District, which includes Montgomery County High School, serves the whole county. Midpoint values near $172,200 mean a clean, repaired house competes well, and one with open tax or lien questions tends to stall.

Before listing, pull your last bill and receipt from the sheriff's site, confirm the parcel on the PVA roll, and note any exemption on file. If you split a lot, check with city hall about subdivision rules first.

faqs.q: Who sends the Montgomery County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Sheriff's Office, which can be reached at (859) 498-8704. Call the PVA at (859) 498-8710 only when the assessed value looks wrong.

faqs.q: Is online payment offered by the Montgomery County Sheriff?
faqs.a: No. Bills and receipts can be viewed and printed on the sheriff's site, but payment must be mailed or brought in at 1 Court Street, Suite 4, Mt. Sterling.

faqs.q: What are the penalty periods after December 31 in Montgomery County?
faqs.a: Five percent applies in January, then twenty-one percent runs from February 1 to April 15. Delinquent bills then move to the County Clerk, who adds attorney and clerk fees plus monthly interest.

faqs.q: Is there zoning in Montgomery County outside Mt. Sterling?
faqs.a: There is none countywide. Subdivisions within five miles of Mt. Sterling follow the city's rules, so ask city hall before dividing land.

faqs.q: What does the state homestead exemption take off a Montgomery County home?
faqs.a: $49,100 comes off the assessed figure for the 2025 and 2026 years. Applicants need to be 65 or older, or totally disabled, and file at the PVA.
